title: Kubernetes & Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
description: Deploy, scale, and secure .NET AI microservices on Azure Kubernetes Service with KEDA autoscaling and Workload Identity.

data.text: When an enterprise AI solution scales to dozens of microservices—API gateways, retrieval workers, vector indexers, and evaluation runners—Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) provides the industrial-grade orchestration backbone. AKS manages container scheduling, automated self-healing, rolling updates with zero downtime, and dynamic pod autoscaling based on incoming token traffic.
Production Kubernetes Deployment Manifest for ASP.NET Core
The manifest below defines an enterprise Deployment with liveness/readiness probes, strict CPU/memory resource limits, and Azure Workload Identity integration.

data.title: Kubernetes Deployment & Service Manifest (YAML)
data.content: Configures hardened pods with health probes, non-root security context, and resource quotas:
data.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: learnai-api-deployment
  namespace: production
  labels:
    app: learnai-api
    azure.workload.identity/use: "true"
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: learnai-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: learnai-api
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: learnai-workload-identity-sa
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: acrlearnai.azurecr.io/learnai-api:v1.2.0
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "250m"
            memory: "512Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "1000m"
            memory: "1Gi"
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz/live
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 15
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz/ready
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          runAsNonRoot: true
--- 
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: learnai-api-service
  namespace: production
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: learnai-api
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 8080

data.text: Standard Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) scales only on CPU and memory utilization. However, background document ingestion workers can be idle while 10,000 PDF documents sit in an Azure Service Bus queue. KEDA (Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling) allows AKS pods to scale directly on external event metrics—such as queue depth or HTTP token requests—scaling from 0 to 50 pods instantly when a burst of documents arrives.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: AKS provides self-healing, rolling deployments, and multi-region cluster management
Always define explicit resource requests and limits to prevent noisy-neighbor memory eviction
Configure liveness and readiness probes to ensure traffic only routes to healthy .NET pods
Use Azure Workload Identity to grant pods direct access to Azure OpenAI without static secrets
Leverage KEDA to scale ingestion worker pods dynamically based on Service Bus queue length
data.takeaway: AKS empowers enterprise .NET teams to deploy, scale, and orchestrate complex AI microservice architectures with zero downtime and fine-grained resource control.
